output.subject: Your request for help with your auto loan payment
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for calling us about your auto loan. You told us that you lost your job at the end of August and won't be able to make your $389 payment due on 25 September, and you asked what hardship options might be available. We're very sorry to hear about your job loss, and we appreciate you reaching out early to talk it through with us.

During your call, our representative went over a one-month deferral with you, and you mentioned you would be applying. A hardship application was sent to you after the call. When you're ready, please complete and return it so that it can be considered.

Our Consumer Lending team will review your request and your application, and we will respond within 10 business days. If anything about your situation changes in the meantime, or if you have any questions about the application, please let us know.

We know this is a stressful time, and we're here to help you work through your options.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: This is a hardship request rather than a complaint; the reply is written as a supportive acknowledgment.
Confirm the hardship application was actually sent, and the channel used (email or post).
Decide whether to set out next steps or a return deadline for the application, especially given the 25 September due date.
Check the loan's eligibility for the one-month deferral the representative discussed. The draft does not promise approval.
Decide whether to address late fees or credit reporting if the 25 September payment is missed before a decision is made.
Consider whether other hardship options beyond the deferral should be mentioned.
